what: `on.request.role: <name>` lets an HTTP flow run only for a caller who holds that one role. It requires sign-in by itself (`auth: required` need not be written): a signed-out caller gets 401 `{"error":"Unauthorized"}` and a signed-in caller without the role 403 `{"error":"Forbidden"}`, before any step runs and before the inputs are checked. A flow without `role:` has no role gate (public_flows covers `auth:`). Scheduled and data-event flows have no caller and take no `role:`.
matching: The value is ONE role name, compared exactly (letter case included) with every role the caller holds: the account's own role (`_benmore_users.role`), its unexpired role grants (global ones, and those for the caller's current tenant) and its tenant membership role (groups.role_field) in the current tenant. A flow gate has no role order: `role: editor` does not admit a `manager`. A global admin passes every role gate, so `role: finance` means finance or a global admin. `role: admin` (any letter case) is not matched by name: only a global admin passes it, never a tenant membership role or tenant-scoped grant named admin. api({at:'rbac'}) gotchas says which accounts are global admins and what to write when a tenant's own admins should call the flow.
one_name_only: The gate has no any-of form, unlike an access `role:a,b` mode or a workflow transition's role list. `role: "warehouse,manager"` (or `role: warehouse manager`) is read as one role name that nobody holds, so the flow answers 403 to everyone but a global admin. A write of such a file is accepted with a warning that says so, `benmore check` gives the same warning, and the app logs it as a WARNING line when it loads the file. A YAML list or map (`role: [warehouse, manager]`) is refused when the file is written. Two more gates get the warning. A single name that the app names nowhere, when app.yaml has a `roles:` block: not under roles:, not groups.bootstrap.founding_role or the default of the membership role column, not in an access `role:` or `owner_or_role:` mode or a workflow transition (`admin` and `user` are built in). It is usually a typo, which nobody holds; a tenant role that exists only as data in the membership table is warned about too and can be ignored. And `role: admin` in an app whose tenant members can hold a role named admin (groups.role_field with groups.bootstrap.founding_role: admin, a membership role column that defaults to admin, or `admin` declared under roles:): tenant admins do not pass that gate.
several_roles: Write `auth: required` and refuse in the first step. By the account's own role: `if: ${{ user.role != 'warehouse' && user.role != 'manager' && user.role != 'admin' }}` with `run: respond` and `with: { status: 403, json: { error: forbidden } }` (yaml_example). `${{ user.role }}` is the `_benmore_users.role` column only. To count role grants as well, read them in a SQL step with id `me` and refuse when it returns no row (`if: ${{ !steps.me.outputs.rows }}`): `SELECT id FROM _benmore_users WHERE id = :user_id AND (role IN ('warehouse', 'manager', 'admin') OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM _benmore_user_roles g WHERE g.user_id = _benmore_users.id AND g.role IN ('warehouse', 'manager', 'admin') AND g.group_id IS NULL AND (g.expires_at IS NULL OR datetime(g.expires_at) > datetime('now'))))`. For tenant roles, read the caller's membership row instead: `SELECT id FROM <groups.table> WHERE <groups.key> = :org AND <groups.user_field> = :user_id AND <groups.role_field> IN ('finance', 'org_admin')` with `params: { org: "${{ user.group_id || 0 }}" }`. A signed-in caller with no tenant has no `user.group_id`: the `|| 0` makes the query match no row, where a bare reference fails the step with a 500.
async: `role:` works on a `mode: async` flow: the request is refused with 401 or 403 instead of the 202, and the role is checked again when the job starts (api({at:'async-flows'}) identity). A step cannot refuse the caller there: the 202 is sent before any step runs, and a `respond` step does nothing in the job. For several roles in front of background work, put a synchronous `auth: required` flow in front of it: that flow checks the caller as several_roles shows, queues the work with `run: enqueue` and answers 202 itself with the enqueue step's `job_id`. Gate the queued flow `role: admin`, so that nobody but a global admin calls it directly (enqueue).
where_it_applies: The gate decides every way the flow runs for a caller: the request, the job of a `mode: async` flow, scheduling it (POST /api/_scheduled answers 403), its line in /_internal/flows.json (a caller without the role does not get the flow, so `bm.flows.<name>` is absent for them) and a connector tool that calls it. A job queued by `run: enqueue` has no caller, so the gate does not apply to it. A scoped credential (an API token or Bearer session with explicit scopes) is covered by permissions.
yaml_example:
# flows/pick-stock.yaml - several roles by the account's own role
# (_benmore_users.role): sign-in is required, and the first step refuses.
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/pick-stock
    auth: required
jobs:
  pick:
    steps:
      - if: ${{ user.role != 'warehouse' && user.role != 'manager' && user.role != 'admin' }}
        run: respond
        with: { status: 403, json: { error: forbidden } }
      - run: sql
        with: { query: "INSERT INTO stock_moves (sku, kind, moved_by) VALUES (:sku, 'pick', :user_id)" }
      - run: respond
        with: { status: 201, json: { picked: true } }
